title: An unramified morphism is quasi-finite at every point
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. Then $f$ is quasi-finite at every point $x\in X$ in the sense of [pqf-def-quasifinite] (1): there are an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A=U\subseteq X$ containing $x$ and an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R=V\subseteq S$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$ such that $R\to A$ is of finite type and $x$, viewed as a prime $\mathfrak q\subset A$ over $\mathfrak p\subset R$, is an isolated point of $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))$. In other words, $f$ is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite] (2). (Stacks Project, Morphisms, Lemma 02V5 (lemma-unramified-quasi-finite); proof: Algebra, Lemma 02UR (lemma-unramified-quasi-finite).)
